newsitem.title: USA: Sen. Grams refuses to back Pena for US Energy Dept.
newsitem.headline: Sen. Grams refuses to back Pena for US Energy Dept.

text.p: U.S. Sen. Rod Grams, who wants to abolish the Energy Department, said Tuesday he would not vote for Federico Pena to be Energy Secretary.

"I have decided that a vote for Mr. Pena's confirmation would send the wrong message to the Administration, my colleagues in Congress, and the taxpayers about our efforts to streamline and improve the federal government," the Minnesota Republican said in a statement.
The Senate Energy Committee is set to vote on Pena's nomination Wednesday, and Energy Department officials expect it to be approved.
A spokesman for Grams said he was not attempting to convince other senators to join him in abstaining in the vote.
Grams said his decision to not vote for Pena was directed against the agency, which he has accused of spending billions of dollars without accomplishing much.
"I have yet to hear any compelling argument against these claims or any substantive justification for keeping the DOE open at a cost to the taxpayers of nearly $20 billion each year," he said.
